metaDescription: Six garden sprayers listed at $20 or less, from 48 ounce hand pumps to a 2 gallon tank and a battery powered model, compared on what the cap really buys.
expertTake: The Chapin 20004 is the best under $20 pick because a one gallon translucent tank with a replaceable pump is what most gardens actually need. The Chapin 1002 is the value pick when your jobs are small and you want a dedicated weed bottle. Skip the cheapest battery sprayer here if you plan to run strong chemicals through it, because a pump this cheap has no documented seals.
introParagraphs: A $20 ceiling is enough to buy a perfectly good garden sprayer, as long as you understand what the money covers. It covers a tank, a pump, a nozzle and a trigger. It does not cover a pressure release valve, premium seals or a long hose.

The smart way to shop at this level is to pick by job: a pint sized bottle for spot work, a one gallon tank for beds, a larger tank for a small lawn, or a hose end bottle for feeding. Prices move, and the $20 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so check the live listing before you buy.

products.name: Chapin 20004 1 Gallon Pump Sprayer, funnel top tank
products.description:
At the budget end, a one gallon pump tank is the sweet spot between capacity and weight, and this is the best executed example of it. The translucent tank shows the level at a glance, the funnel top lets you tip a measured cup of concentrate in without a splash, and an anti clog filter protects the nozzle from undissolved particles.

The pump is a standard plunger design that you can rebuild with a small seal kit, which is a bigger deal at this price than it sounds. A sprayer you can repair outlasts several you throw away. It is also cheap enough to dedicate to weed killer. Against the 1.3 gallon Amazon Basics it has less capacity but a better known service record, and against the 48 ounce Chapin 1002 it holds more than twice the liquid.

What you give up at this price is a relief valve, a trigger lock and a hose. Release pressure by squeezing the trigger before opening, rinse after each use, and let the tank dry with the cap off so mildew does not form. When the stream weakens, give it a few more strokes rather than waiting for it to cough, because a fully empty pump draws air and can lose its prime.
products.bestFor: Most gardeners who want one dependable sprayer for beds and weeds.
pros: Rebuildable plunger pump with cheap seals
Clear tank shows the level at a glance
Cheap enough to dedicate to herbicide
cons: Pressure fades as the tank empties

products.name: Chapin 1002 48 oz Hand Pump Sprayer for lawn and garden
products.description:
This is the cheapest tank in the lineup, and for the right job it is also the most sensible. A 48 ounce tank is a bottle you pressurize, not a tank you carry, so it suits pots, a few raised beds and the odd patch of weeds. The wide mouth makes filling and scrubbing easy, and the cone nozzle adjusts from a mist to a stream.

The small volume is its limit: a single fill treats a small area, and you will refill often. But the price is so low that it works well as a dedicated bottle for one chemical, which is the best way to avoid cross contamination. Against the Chapin 20004 it holds less than half the liquid and costs less, and against the Amazon Basics it lacks the extension wand.

Because the pump is small, a stiff stroke usually means a dry seal. A drop of silicone grease fixes it, and the bottle itself is cheap to replace if it cracks. Rinse after use and keep it from freezing. One neat trick is to keep two of these side by side, one with a colored band of tape for herbicide, because at this price a second bottle is cheaper than one scorched rose bush.
products.bestFor: Pots, small beds and a dedicated spot treatment bottle.
pros: Wide mouth is easy to fill and clean
Cheap enough to dedicate to one chemical

products.name: Amazon Basics 1.3 Gallon Pump Garden Sprayer, extension wand
products.description:
What you get here that the cheapest tanks leave out is the extension wand and a thumb trigger with a continuous on position. The wand lets you reach under shrubs and across a bed without bending, and the continuous on setting lets your hand relax during a long pass. The tank is a translucent 1.3 gallons with a funnel top.

The twist nozzle moves from a narrow stream to a wide shower, which is flexible but not precise. It lacks the anti clog filter detail that the Chapin lists, so keep an eye on the screen in the shut off. The extra capacity makes it a little heavier when full, around ten pounds, so fill it only as much as you need.

As with all budget tanks, the seals are standard rather than documented chemical resistant. Use it with label rate mixes, rinse thoroughly and check the lid gasket at the start of each season.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want reach and a lock on spray at a budget price.
pros: Larger tank than the one gallon models
cons: No documented filter or seal detail

products.name: Chapin 20005 2 Gallon Pump Sprayer, funnel top
products.description:
If your yard is bigger than a few beds, the two gallon capacity is the reason to stretch to this sprayer. It uses the same plunger pump and funnel top as the one gallon Chapin, scaled up, so a fertilizer pass over a small lawn or a fence line fits in a single fill instead of two.

The cost is weight and effort. Two gallons is about sixteen pounds, and a bigger air space takes more strokes to pressurize. Against the Chapin 20004 you gain capacity and lose comfort, and compared with the Lovydro battery sprayer you work harder but spend less on a design with no battery to go flat.

The pump rebuilds with a seal kit, and the tank is translucent so you can read the level. Rinse after every use, avoid pressurizing to the point where the pump head locks, and store it dry. It earns its place as the capacity option under the cap.
products.bestFor: Small lawns and long borders that need more than a gallon per fill.
pros: Two gallons covers a small lawn per fill
Anti clog filter protects the nozzle

products.name: Chapin G390 32 Ounce Hose End Sprayer for Fertilizer
products.description:
A hose end sprayer is a different tool from a pump tank, and for lawn feeding it is often a better one. You fill the 32 ounce bottle with water soluble concentrate, screw it on a garden hose and the passing water pulls product through a metering orifice, so there is no pump to work and no bucket to mix.

The listing describes a chemical resistant poly tank, a universal hose fit and a fingertip on off control. It meters at a ratio set by the head, which is the limit: you cannot dial it, so match your fertilizer to the head. Next to the Chapin 20004 it covers lawns far faster, but it needs a tap, and it gives you less control around plants you do not want to feed.

After every use, flush clean water through the bottle and head until it runs clear, and store it with the cap off. Dried fertilizer in the head is the most common cause of a blocked bottle.
products.bestFor: Quick lawn feeding from a garden hose with no pumping.
cons: One fixed ratio from the head
Needs a hose and tap within reach

products.name: Lovydro 2 Gallon Battery Powered Sprayer, 3 speeds, 4 nozzles
products.description:
It is unusual to see a battery powered sprayer under a $20 ceiling, and the appeal is obvious: one trigger press and the spray runs at steady pressure, with no pumping at all. Three speeds are shown on a display, and a battery indicator tells you how much runtime is left. A four foot hose has a filter head that strains debris before the pump.

The compromises are the ones you expect at this level. The pump is small, the brand has a short track record and there is no documented chemical resistance, so keep it to fertilizer, soap and plant care and avoid strong herbicides. Four mist nozzles suit foliar spray but give no wide fan for lawns. Compared with the Chapin 20005 it saves effort and costs about the same, but you accept a less proven pump.

Flush it with clean water after every use, because salts crystallize in a small diaphragm pump. An empty tank stored indoors over winter keeps the seals from drying out and the pump from freezing. Because the pump is sealed, a failure usually means replacement, so treat the low cost as the price of convenience and not as a promise of a decade of service.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who dislike pumping and mainly mist and feed plants.
pros: Filter head strains debris before the pump
cons: Unproven pump life at this level

buyingCriteria.explanation: Under $20 you get a working tank, pump and nozzle, and you do not get Viton seals, a relief valve or a hose. The Chapin 20004 is a good example of the format. If you spray strong chemicals often, plan to spend more or to replace the seals yourself, since standard rubber swells with some herbicides.

The Lovydro 2 Gallon removes the pumping, and the Chapin 20005 asks for many strokes to pressurize two gallons. A battery pump holds even pressure but adds a battery that can fade, and small pumps can fail sooner. For jobs under a quarter hour, manual tanks are simpler and last longer.

A gallon of liquid is about eight pounds, so the Chapin 20005 at two gallons is around sixteen. The Chapin 1002 at 48 ounces is about three. Budget buyers often take the biggest tank and then stop using it because it is heavy. Pick the size that suits your longest single job.

A rebuildable pump with a cheap seal kit turns a low cost sprayer into a long lived one. The Chapin pump tanks use standard plunger seals that you can replace, whereas many battery handles are sealed units. At this price, repairability matters more than any extra feature.

A funnel top or wide mouth saves spills and makes scrubbing easy. The Chapin 1002 wide mouth and the funnel top on the Chapin 20004 both help. A tank that is hard to rinse gets neglected, and a neglected sprayer clogs.

At this price you can afford more than one sprayer. Keeping a cheap tank for herbicide and another for plant feed prevents cross contamination, which is the commonest cause of scorched plants. Label each with tape.

specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Lovydro here uses a battery pump.

howWeEvaluated.title: Price and listing
howWeEvaluated.description: Only items whose live listing price was at or below the cap on the day of the update were considered. We did not quote any product price, since prices move and a stale number misleads.

howWeEvaluated.title: Repairability
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored units on whether the pump can be rebuilt and the seals replaced. The Chapin plunger tanks scored highest, and the sealed battery handle scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: Tank volume was converted to full weight. The Chapin 1002 at about three pounds is the lightest, and the Chapin 20005 at about sixteen the heaviest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience features
howWeEvaluated.description: Wand, thumb trigger, funnel top and display features were counted. The Amazon Basics extension wand and the Lovydro display added points, based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns.

howWeEvaluated.title: Chemical suitability
howWeEvaluated.description: None of the six documents Viton seals, so each was scored for label rate use. The Chapin G390 lists a chemical resistant poly tank for water soluble products.

cards.label: Manual pump
cards.text: Cheap, simple and rebuildable, but you pump and the pressure sags. Picks: Chapin 20004, Chapin 1002, Amazon Basics 1.3 Gallon and Chapin 20005.

cards.label: Battery
cards.text: No pumping and steady pressure, but a small pump of unproven life. Pick: Lovydro 2 Gallon.

howToChoose.note: Choose manual if you spray briefly and want it to last, and battery if pumping is the problem.

rows: Cheap enough to label and keep separate
Four mist nozzles and a filter head

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A translucent tank, a replaceable seal and a funnel top. Avoid hype about pressure numbers and buy the size you can carry.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Chapin 20004 is the safest first sprayer, and the Chapin 1002 is a small second bottle for a different chemical.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You spray herbicide often, want a relief valve or need a long hose. Look above the cap for chemical resistant seals.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You spray occasionally. A Chapin 20004 or 1002 does the job within the cap.

maintenance.why: Residue dries into crystals that clog filters and attack seals. Three rinses keep a budget sprayer working.
Squeeze the trigger until the hiss stops. Opening a pressurized tank can splash liquid at your face.
A dry seal makes the stroke stiff and leaky. A little silicone grease restores it.
Fertilizer salts clog the nozzle. Rinse and clear it with a soft pin.
Water in a tank can freeze and crack it. Drain and store it inside.

faq.q: Is a $20 garden sprayer good enough?
faq.a: Yes, for most home gardens. A one gallon pump tank handles beds, weeds and light lawn work. The limits are seals and extras, so use label rate mixes and check seals each season.
The Chapin pump tanks, because their pumps are rebuildable with cheap seals. A sealed battery handle is harder to repair.

faq.q: Can I use these for strong weed killer?
faq.a: They use standard seals, so follow the label and watch for swelling. For frequent herbicide use, buy a sprayer with chemical resistant seals above the cap.
Not always. Prices move, and the cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so check the live listing.

faq.q: Is a battery sprayer under $20 reliable?
faq.a: It saves effort, but the pump is small and unproven. Keep it to feeding and misting, and flush it after every use.

faq.q: What size should I buy first?
faq.a: A one gallon tank is the best first size. Add a small bottle for spot jobs later.
